headline: 3 police officers sentenced to death for July crimes against humanity
summary: The International Crimes Tribunal-1 has published the full verdict for the Rampura and Banasree area atrocities, detailing the roles of former police officials in the deaths of protesters.
details: The International Crimes Tribunal-1 has released the full 147-page verdict in the crimes against humanity case involving atrocities in the Rampura and Banasree areas of Dhaka during the July uprising.
Former DMP Commissioner Habibur Rahman, former Khilgaon zone ADC Mo. Rashedul Islam, and former Rampura OC Mo. Mashiur Rahman were all sentenced to death. All three are currently fugitives.
The verdict details that former OC Mashiur Rahman led the brutality in the area, and personally shot victims including Maya Islam and Nadim Hussein, both of whom were killed.

The tribunal found that the protesters and general public were unarmed. Former Commissioner Habibur Rahman had ordered his subordinates via radio to use maximum force without hesitation against the protesters.
caption:
Three former police officials, including a former DMP Commissioner, have been sentenced to death for crimes against humanity during the July uprising.

The International Crimes Tribunal-1 has released the full 147-page verdict in the crimes against humanity case involving atrocities in the Rampura and Banasree areas of Dhaka during the July uprising.

Former DMP Commissioner Habibur Rahman, former Khilgaon zone ADC Mo. Rashedul Islam, and former Rampura OC Mo. Mashiur Rahman were all sentenced to death. All three are currently fugitives.

The verdict details that former OC Mashiur Rahman led the brutality in the area, and personally shot victims including Maya Islam and Nadim Hussein, both of whom were killed.

The tribunal found that the protesters and general public were unarmed. Former Commissioner Habibur Rahman had ordered his subordinates via radio to use maximum force without hesitation against the protesters.

Source: Dhaka Tribune, Prothom Alo

headline_marked: Saudi Arabia [[keen to invest $1 billion in port management]] in Bangladesh
headline: Saudi Arabia keen to invest $1 billion in port management in Bangladesh
summary: A high-level Saudi delegation met with Prime Minister Tarique Rahman to discuss expanding bilateral cooperation in infrastructure and investment.
details: A high-level Saudi Arabian delegation, led by Deputy Minister of Transport and Logistics Services Rumaih Mohammad Al-Rumaih, met with Prime Minister Tarique Rahman at the Prime Minister's Office in the National Parliament Building on Wednesday.

The delegation expressed interest in increasing their investment in Bangladesh's port management to $1 billion, including a $180 million investment by Red Sea Gateway Terminal International for the construction of a bay terminal.
Beyond port management, Red Sea Gateway Terminal International and other Saudi entities expressed interest in investing in various other sectors of the economy.
Prime Minister Tarique Rahman informed the delegation about the investment-friendly policies and initiatives of his government to encourage foreign direct investment.
The Saudi representatives noted that they have already assessed the potential for investment in ports, railways, and other infrastructure sectors.
Both sides discussed strengthening bilateral ties and expanding cooperation in infrastructure development, with a potential joint meeting to be held in the future for detailed discussions.
caption:
Saudi Arabia is looking to scale up its investment in Bangladesh's port management to $1 billion.

A high-level Saudi Arabian delegation, led by Deputy Minister of Transport and Logistics Services Rumaih Mohammad Al-Rumaih, met with Prime Minister Tarique Rahman at the Prime Minister's Office in the National Parliament Building on Wednesday.

The delegation expressed interest in increasing their investment in Bangladesh's port management to $1 billion, including a $180 million investment by Red Sea Gateway Terminal International for the construction of a bay terminal.

Beyond port management, Red Sea Gateway Terminal International and other Saudi entities expressed interest in investing in various other sectors of the economy.

Prime Minister Tarique Rahman informed the delegation about the investment-friendly policies and initiatives of his government to encourage foreign direct investment.

The Saudi representatives noted that they have already assessed the potential for investment in ports, railways, and other infrastructure sectors.

Both sides discussed strengthening bilateral ties and expanding cooperation in infrastructure development, with a potential joint meeting to be held in the future for detailed discussions.

Source: Prothom Alo, Jamuna TV
